title: German Maternal Mortality and Stillbirth Registry: A National Registry for Maternal Deaths and Stillbirths in Germany
summary:
Maternal deaths and stillbirths are among the most serious adverse events associated with pregnancy and childbirth. Although relatively rare in Germany, they can have a profound and lasting impact on families, healthcare professionals, and the healthcare system.

The GeMoRe Registry collects nationwide data on these events to improve understanding of their causes and to identify opportunities for improving maternity care. The knowledge gained from this registry is intended to contribute to safer care for pregnant women and their babies and to support efforts to prevent avoidable deaths.

Data collection is based exclusively on pseudonymised information and does not influence the medical care provided to affected individuals.
conditions: Maternal mortality; late maternal mortality; pregnancy-associated mortality; stillbirth; perinatal mortality.

interventions.name: Single-arm observational registry cohort. All maternal deaths and stillbirths reported to the GeMoRe registry are included. No intervention is applied. Data are collected prospectively as part of a nationwide observational surveillance registry.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Case reported by a participating maternity unit, perinatal centre, or collaborating healthcare institution
Availability of sufficient clinical information for documentation within the registry
Pseudonymised data collection in accordance with registry requirements
Maternal deaths according to the World Health Organization (WHO) definition (death during pregnancy or within 42 days following termination of pregnancy, irrespective of the duration or site of the pregnancy)
Late maternal deaths (>42 days and <1 year after the end of pregnancy) may be recorded and analysed separately
Stillbirths according to the definitions applicable in Germany at the time of registration
Exclusion criteria:
Cases that do not meet the definition of either a maternal death or a stillbirth
Miscarriages according to the legal definitions applicable in Germany
Live births without documented intrauterine fetal death
Duplicate reports of the same event
Cases with insufficient data quality preventing classification according to the registry criteria

Accidental or incidental causes of death unrelated to pregnancy may be recorded within the registry but will be analysed separately from maternal deaths as defined by the WHO.
